ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, with $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, fold $\triangle CBD$ along CD, so that point B precisely lands on point E on side AC. If $\angle A=22^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle EDA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle A=22^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle B=90^\circ-\angle A=68^\circ$,\\
By the property of folding, we have: $\angle CED=\angle B=68^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle EDA=\angle CED-\angle A=\boxed{46^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle A=22^\circ$,\\ thus $\angle B=90^\circ-\angle A=68^\circ$,\\ By the property of folding, we have $\angle CED=\angle B=68^\circ$,\\ therefore $\angle EDA=\angle CED-\angle A=\boxed{46^\circ}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, B is at the lower left, A is at the lower right, and BA is a horizontal base; C is at the upper left, CA is a side slanting toward the lower right, and a right-angle mark is drawn at C. D is located on line segment BA, and E is located on line segment CA; in the figure there is a dashed line from C to D, indicating crease CD, and line segment DE is drawn from D to E, indicating the side formed after B is folded to E. Reasoning: It is known that ∠ACB=90°, ∠A=22°, so in triangle ABC, ∠ABC=180°-90°-22°=68°. Because D is on BA, ∠CBD is the same as ∠ABC, being 68°. Fold triangle CBD along CD so that B lands on E, while C and D remain fixed, therefore ∠CBD before folding corresponds to ∠CED after folding, so ∠CED=68°. Also because E is on AC, EC and EA are opposite rays on the same straight line, and AD is on AB, ∠CED is the exterior angle at E of triangle ADE, therefore ∠CED=∠DAE+∠EDA. ∠DAE is ∠A=22°, so ∠EDA=68°-22°=46°.
